**Proposed mechanism:** SCN4A (HGNC:10595) —DISRUPTS→ Gain-of-function variant in SCN4A; Gain-of-function variant in SCN4A —DISRUPTS→ Skeletal muscle sodium channel activity (GO:0005255); Skeletal muscle sodium channel activity (GO:0005255) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis (MONDO:0008224); SCN1B (HGNC:10596) —DISRUPTS→ Loss-of-function variant in SCN1B; Loss-of-function variant in SCN1B —DISRUPTS→ Skeletal muscle sodium channel activity (GO:0005255); Skeletal muscle sodium channel activity (GO:0005255) —LEADS_TO→ Brugada syndrome 5 (MONDO:0013015). Gain-of-function variants in SCN4A lead to impaired fast inactivation of skeletal muscle sodium channels, causing hyperkalemic periodic paralysis. Loss-of-function variants in SCN1B (which co-assembles with SCN4A or other sodium channel alpha subunits) can similarly impair sodium channel function, leading to Brugada syndrome 5.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the causal variants for hyperkalemic periodic paralysis in SCN4A do not affect fast inactivation of the sodium channel, or that variants for Brugada syndrome 5 in SCN1B do not impair sodium channel function, or that the two gene products function in entirely separate cellular compartments or pathways with no overlap in their downstream effects on excitability. _(variant: Presence of common variants (e.g., >1% allele frequency in gnomAD) in SCN4A or SCN1B associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of sodium channel subunits in these distinct channelopathies could reveal common therapeutic targets for modulating ion channel function, potentially applicable to both skeletal muscle and cardiac conditions.
